Sally Season Ep. 14 🥖 Banh Mi Salad

Ingredients: 
* Stale bread - 150g
* Pork belly - 500g
* Soy sauce
* Fish sauce
* Garlic - 1 cloves
* Honey
* Carrots - 1
* Cucumber - 1
* Spring onion - 4
* Rice wine vinegar
* Limes - 2
* Coriander - 10g
* Red chilli - 1 
* Kewpie mayo
* Sriracha 

1. Preheat the oven to 200°C
2. Cut the stale bread into cubes. Add to a tray with a sprinkle of salt and a glug of olive oil. Mix well and place in the oven for 15-20 minutes.
3. Add 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp honey, 2 tsp fish sauce and 1 grated cloves of garlic to a bowl and mix well. And the pork and massage then set aside. 
4. Place a pan on medium high heat with 1 tbsp oil. Add the pork belly slices. Turn when they get a bit of colour on one side. Once they’ve got a bit of colour on both sides, transfer to an oven proof dish, add any of the remaining marinating liquid into the tray and place in the oven for 15 minutes.
5. Cut one carrot and the cucumber into thin matchsticks. Finely slice 4 spring onions. Add all of them to a bowl along with 2 tbsp rice wine vinegar and the juice of 2 limes. Mix well and set aside.
6. Thinly slice one red chili and chop the coriander roughly and set aside ready to assemble the salad. 
7. Make the dressing by combining 1 tbsp kewpie mayo, 1 tbsp sriracha, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tsp fish sauce and 1 tbsp olive oil. I also reduce any liquid left in the tray with the pork and add that to the dressing for even more flavour. 
8. Slice the pork into thin strips. Add it to the bowl with the carrots etc. along with the red chilli, coriander, croutons and half the dressing.
9. Mix everything together thoroughly then serve up. Finish with an extra drizzle of dressing

I’m a traditional viet girlie so I’ve always loved Banh Mi Cha Lua (pork roll) with extra pate and veggies on side. You can order other banh mis that range from $5-7 depending on the protein.

✨ Pro Tips: 
1️⃣ Ask for extra pate in all your sandwiches.
2️⃣ Ask for veggies on side. You can then add however much pickled veggies, jalapeno, cilantro, or cucumbers you want - plus it doesn’t make the banh mi soggy especially when it’s only takeout.
3️⃣ Go before 10AM or after 1PM to avoid long lines or rush hour
4️⃣ If you want other foods besides banh mi, make sure to go before noon (more fresh and they sell out)

They have a variety of other Vietnamese foods there that are also on the low low - banh cuon, spring rolls, eggrolls, pandan waffles, che, Vietnamese coffee, and more. Whenever I miss home back in Orange County, I come here for my viet cravings 🥺❤️
